LESSON: COOKING: USING FLOUR MIXTURES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Food Production Processes
Topic 2.3: Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures, part of Food Production Processes in Grade 9 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How can we make products from flour mixtures?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify types of flour mixtures used in food production

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. prepare flour mixtures for food production

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make products from various flour mixtures

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate products made from various flour mixtures. Learners are guided to: • use print or digital resources to identify types of flour mixtures used in food production such as batters and dough. • prepare flour mixtures such as batters and doughs for food production. • make products such as pancakes, mandazi, and chapati from various flour mixtures. • display and appreciate the products made from various flour mixtures. How can we make products from flour mixtures?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify types of flour mixtures used in food production

   Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. prepare flour mixtures for food production

   Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. make products from various flour mixtures

   Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate products made from various flour mixtures. Learners are guided to: • use print or digital resources to identify types of flour mixtures used in food production such as batters and dough. • prepare flour mixtures such as batters and doughs for food production. • make products such as pancakes, mandazi, and chapati from various flour mixtures. • display and appreciate the products made from various flour mixtures. How can we make products from flour mixtures?

   Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to Learn: reflection on own work as learners apply procedures of preparing flour mixtures.

Values:
Integrity: following ethically acceptable procedures in preparing flour mixtures.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Safety of self and others as learners use tools and fuels in making products from flour mixtures.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Learners relate the measurement of ingredients in preparing flour mixtures to weights and measurements learnt in Mathematics.
